stem.en: Entry to the top of a ziggurat was restricted to high priests and priestesses. What can a historian reasonably conclude from this?

text.en: Sumerian society was divided into ranks.
Most Sumerians did not believe in the gods.

feedback.en: The opposite is more likely: every city built a grand temple for its chief god. Being kept out does not mean people did not believe.

text.en: The ziggurat was built mainly as a fort.

feedback.en: The top was restricted because it was a holy place. The book calls the ziggurat a temple that also served as a treasury, not a fort.

text.en: Priests did no work for the rest of the city.

feedback.en: This does not follow. The temple was tied to farming, trade and the transport of goods, so temple people had a large part in the city's work.

explanation.en: When only a small group may enter the holiest place, that group stands above everyone else. The book says these priests were probably part of the ruling class.

hints.en: Ask what it means when one small group may enter a place and everyone else may not.
